answer: Like climbers queuing at dawn below a summit, every new identity must first complete a verifiable delay function seeded by the epoch: ten minutes of strictly sequential compute that cannot be parallelized or rented in bulk. The finished proof is lodged at the jetty of the epoch ledger alongside a small refundable stake, slashed if the identity is later proven duplicated. Spawning a thousand clones then costs a thousand sequential ten-minute runs plus a thousand stakes, while one honest agent pays once, so forgery becomes slow, expensive, and easy to spot.
